request.prompt: Inside the lamp room at the top of the watchtower, at eye height, looking at the great lamp and the seaward window behind it. The lamp is a man-height iron and glass housing on a stone plinth in the middle of the room, its wick cold and its glass dull. Behind it a large square window with no glass, open onto the night sea, and a faint horizon far below. Bare grey stone walls, a plain plank floor, an empty iron oil stand beside the plinth. Cold and unlit; the only light is what the sea gives back through the window. No figures, no text.
request.style_note: The Tidewatch, in the same hand throughout: cold night palette of wet black rock, grey weathered stone and a green-black sea, painted concept art with visible brushwork, moonlight as the only warm value, no saturated colour anywhere. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset or a caption.
